$doc: SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for bento slot geometry. Read by components/bento.tsx (via lib/bento-slots.ts) AND by the bento-crop skill's crop.py retina-floor check. Do NOT fork these numbers into either consumer — change them here and both the render math and the crop floor move together.

container.note: .cs-section-pinned: inside .case-study-prose > .cs-section the prose caps at 660px below 1024px; the section breaks out to min(100vw-4rem, 1088px) at >=1024px. A bento in a WIDER or NARROWER container renders at different widths, which changes every derived floor. Re-measure and add a container variant here before trusting floors elsewhere.

retina.note: Source floor = dpr * maxRenderedWidthPx. Bump to 3 only if 3x-DPR delivery is required.

wide.note: MAX is the md 660px 1-up render, NOT the 536px desktop 2-up width — the trap.

breakouts.note: N:1 strips (BentoBand, BentoRibbon), full container width at >=768px. Ribbon below 768px = fixed-height horizontal-scroll canvas: width = ribbonTrackHeightPx * N. For steep N that exceeds the container (crossover N = maxWidthPx/ribbonTrackHeightPx = 1088/80 = 13.6), so the floor uses max(container, mobileCanvas). The aspect N comes from the crop-spec output's `aspect` field, not from here.
breakouts.mobileLegibilityFloorNote: The retina floor guards source pixels, not readability. A NON-SCROLLING band below ~110px rendered height is texture, not information. At the 326px mobile container (390px viewport minus the 4rem .case-study-prose inset) ~110px is roughly a 3:1 aspect, so a non-scrolling band steeper than ~3:1 goes illegible on mobile and needs a scrollFloor (BentoBand's mobile scroll track), a mobile-specific crop, or a shallower cut. Measured on BARD: 2.63 -> 124px legible; 3.13 -> 104px texture; 5.54 -> 59px; 11.37 -> 29px (the KPI strip, now scrollFloored to 1088). Ribbons are exempt: they carry a 128px min-height floor and scroll natively.
